key_insights: US equities rose on the week after two down days: SPX +59bps to 7811 (9/11 sectors up, Real Estate +1.88%, Consumer Disc. +1.69%, Communication Svcs. -0.40%), NDX +51bps to 30,883 (up 6 of the last 7 weeks), RTY +46bps to 2806.
AI Software (GSTMTAIS) rose 513bps while telcos sold off, with TMUS -13.3% following SPCX +1.3% spectrum acquisition headlines.

Flow: Asset managers were moderate net sellers and hedge funds balanced. Oil and rate volatility plus anticipation into earnings kept client activity low for most of the week. The desk saw a heavy wave of selling in Semis and AI around OpenAI revenue headlines on Thursday that continued Friday despite the clarification.

Q3 EPS preview: consensus is +27% y/y, the highest estimate since 2021, while the median stock is at 9% y/y (vs 14% in Q2). Last quarter beats stayed historically frequent but were rewarded with one of the smallest outperformances vs the S&P on record (35bps vs 95bps historically).
Mag7 positioning on the Prime book moved from YTD lows in June (14% of US exposure) to a record high of 22%, after Mag7 had its most volatile quarter on record in Q2.

Hedge fund update: fundamental L/S managers were down 0.2% last week (alpha -0.3%) and are up 12.5% YTD. Gross leverage rose 3.3 pts to 209.5% (43rd percentile over 1 year). Net leverage fell 0.2 pts to 52.9% (6th percentile over 1 year).

The global hedge fund book was net sold, driven by EM and North America. Europe was the only net bought region, for a 4th consecutive week. Info Tech and Communication Services were the most net sold sectors (Communication Services for a 3rd consecutive week), while Industrials and Consumer Discretionary were the most net bought. Turnover was low.

John Flood argues the S&P 500 could pierce 8k in short order, citing corporate demand, negative investor sentiment, low net hedge fund exposure, possible supercap IPOs exciting retail investors, and a strong earnings season.

Cross-asset: GS moves back to overweight equities for 3 months (in line with 12 months), citing earnings growth support and improved asymmetry after the recent valuation de-rating. GS moves overweight bonds for 12 months on better medium-term value in long-duration bonds as inflation normalizes and central bank pricing turns less hawkish. Tactically it still prefers shorter-duration fixed income (overweight cash).
Basket idea: POWER UP AMERICA (GSENEPOW) is the preferred AI-related expression, since power supply, grid capacity and gas infrastructure remain constraints on datacenter buildout.

EU Real Estate 3Q26 preview: GS cuts 2026E NTAs by 6% and downgrades AT1 to Sell. Debate is expected to center on capital allocation, disposals and leverage, with stronger balance sheets or high-yielding acquisitions better placed to grow earnings.

TRYG (DC) upgraded to Neutral on inflecting growth and improving operational KPIs. The stock has underperformed the sector by about 17% YTD and the broader market by about 20%, on decelerating top-line growth and AI and autonomous vehicle concerns.

ASML is reportedly (unconfirmed) raising prices on all EUV and DUV spare parts in Korea by 10%, accepted by Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix for deliveries from January 2027. Services, parts and upgrades were about 25% of 2025 revenue and are expected to grow by more than 30% in 2026. GS calls this positive ahead of Wednesday's results.
